subject: [PATCH 2/3] blk-iocost: clear delay state when freeing policy data

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Raised concern about potential conflicts between different policies, specifically io.latency and io.cost, when clearing delay state. Suggested checking if iocost had actually set a delay before clearing it.

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary: Dismissed the concern, stating that the two mechanisms are not usually used together and even when they conflict, clearing use_delay spuriously is transient and harmless.
reviews.raw_body:
> Does this unconditional call to blkcg_clear_delay() overwrite state managed
> by other policies?
> 
> Since use_delay is shared among block cgroup policies, if iocost never
> actually applied a delay, this might forcefully zero out the delay state
> managed by other active policies like blk-iolatency. 
> 
> Would it be safer to check if iocost had actually set a delay before clearing
> it here?

Yeah, this is fine. The two mechanisms aren't usually used together and even
when they step on each other, use_delay being cleared spuriously is
transient and nothing really breaks.

Thanks.

-- 
tejun

2026-08-10.patch_summary: The patch aims to clear delay state when freeing policy data, but a reviewer raised concerns about potential conflicts between different policies.
